question_text: WTO aims at
explanation: 'The WTO … regulates international trade,' opening telecom markets to competition and investment — it liberalises international (not domestic) trade.

question_text: All the following are rules or guidelines contained in the WTO Reference Paper on Regulation EXCEPT
options: There should be a regulatory body independent of governments and operating companies
Licensing criteria should be publicly available and transparent
The regulator should allocate scarce resources fairly between operators
Regulation should provide for interconnection between major operators
correct_answer: There should be a regulatory body independent of governments and operating companies
explanation: The Reference Paper requires a regulator 'independent of operating companies (but not necessarily of governments)'. So requiring independence from governments as well overstates it — that option is the exception; (b), (c) and (d) are genuine Reference-Paper principles.

question_text: Characteristics of ______ include the removal of exclusive rights from monopoly firms and award of licences for all new services on a competitive basis.
explanation: Liberalization = 'the removal of exclusive rights from the former monopoly … and the award of licences for all new services on a competitive basis.'

question_text: In a de-regulated industry, market forces are allowed to work with no external intervention.
explanation: The deck equates the terms: 'industries with zero regulation … are also said to be completely deregulated (i.e. regulation has been completely removed),' with no external intervention. (The mid-sem key left this un-highlighted, so confirm with your lecturer.)

question_text: The process of transition from a monopoly market to a competitive one is referred to as ______.
explanation: 'Liberalization … represents the process of transition from a monopoly market to a competitive one.'

question_text: Two linear equations A and B represent two supply curves. A has a slope of 2 while B has a slope of 3. Which of the two equations represent a more elastic supply?
explanation: Under the usual convention a flatter supply curve (smaller slope in the price–quantity plane) is more elastic, so A (slope 2) is taken as more elastic than B. NB: slope alone doesn't strictly fix supply elasticity — the mid-sem key left this un-highlighted, so verify the intended answer.

question_text: The following are instruments of regulation EXCEPT
explanation: The decks list regulations, decisions, policies AND resolutions all as regulatory instruments, so every option is an instrument and none is the exception.

question_text: ______ refers to the intervention by governments in markets in order to achieve certain outcomes in those markets.
explanation: 'Regulation … refers to the intervention by governments in markets in order to achieve certain outcomes in those markets.'

question_text: Supply is the quantity of a good sellers wish to sell each time the market opens.
explanation: FALSE. Supply is the whole price–quantity relationship (the supply schedule / curve), not one fixed amount. The deck calls the amount sellers will sell at a given price the 'quantity supplied'. (Highlighted FALSE in the mid-sem key.)

question_text: Which form of regulation establishes a common and legally enforceable platform for all businesses within a sector?
explanation: 'Technical standardisation … establishes a common and legally enforceable platform for all businesses within a sector.'

question_text: A market can accurately be described as
options: the process by which prices adjust to reconcile the allocation of resources
a place where buyers and sellers meet
correct_answer: a place where buyers and sellers meet
explanation: The deck defines a market as 'a group of buyers and sellers of a particular good or service' — i.e. where buyers and sellers meet. (Highlighted (d) in the mid-sem key.)

question_text: ______ regulation states, in advance, a rule that a company must obey.
options: nemo judex in sua causa debet esse
explanation: A rule stated in advance that a company must obey is ex-ante regulation (ex ante = 'before certain issues arise').

question_text: Which one of the following does NOT occur in perfect competition?
options: Firms and buyers are completely informed about the prices of the products of each firm in the industry.
There are significant restrictions on entry into the industry.
Firms already in the industry have no advantage over potential new entrants.
No single firm can exert a significant influence on the market price of the good.
correct_answer: There are significant restrictions on entry into the industry.
explanation: Perfect competition has free entry, so 'significant restrictions on entry' does NOT occur; the other options all do.

question_text: An increase in consumer income will increase demand for a/an ______ but decrease demand for a/an ______.
explanation: For a normal good, demand rises as income rises; for an inferior good, demand falls as income rises. So income up → more of a normal good, less of an inferior good.

question_text: The factors that encouraged the monopoly paradigm in the telecommunication sector can be categorized as
explanation: The deck names exactly two factors behind the state-monopoly era: Economic (natural monopoly) and Political (state control). 'Social' is not listed.

question_text: Which of the following is NOT a widely accepted regulatory objective in the telecommunication sector?
options: Foster competitive markets to promote local entrepreneurial initiative
Protect consumer rights, including privacy rights
Promote universal access to basic telecommunications services
Create a favourable climate to promote investment to expand telecommunications networks
correct_answer: Foster competitive markets to promote local entrepreneurial initiative
explanation: The deck's objective is to foster competitive markets to promote efficient supply, quality, advanced services and efficient prices — NOT 'local entrepreneurial initiative'. The other four are listed objectives verbatim.

question_text: What type of rule is referred to as 'common sense' regulation?
options: nemo judex in sua causa debet esse
explanation: Inferred: 'common-sense' regulation best fits ex-post — general principles applied with judgment after the fact. NB: the phrase is not verbatim in the decks and the mid-sem key left it un-highlighted, so confirm with your lecturer.

question_text: The mission of the UN specialized agency responsible for issues concerning information and communication technologies includes all of the following EXCEPT
options: coordinating the shared global use of the radio spectrum
promoting international cooperation in assigning satellite orbits
working to improve telecommunication infrastructure in the developing world
assisting in the development and coordination of worldwide technical standards
explanation: The deck gives the ITU mission as exactly these four, so all are included and none is the exception.

question_text: Perfect competition occurs in a market where there are many firms each selling
explanation: Under perfect competition 'the goods offered for sale are all exactly the same' — i.e. an identical (homogeneous) product.

question_text: The maxim 'hear the other side' is expressed in Latin as
options: nemo judex in sua causa debet esse
explanation: 'Hear the other side' is the maxim audi alteram partem — the fair-hearing rule.

question_text: Which of these entities is responsible for policy implementation in the telecommunication sector in most developed market economies?
options: The ministry in charge of the telecommunication sector
explanation: Policy-making is the ministry's (political) role; 'regulation focuses on translating the objectives of policy decisions into practical measures' — so the independent national regulator implements policy. (Un-highlighted in the key.)

question_text: Which of the following is FALSE about an industry with one monopoly firm?
explanation: The deck lists exactly three monopoly harms: lower output (low supply), higher price, and less-efficient/higher-cost production. 'Inferior goods are produced' is not one of them — so it is the false statement.

question_text: Which of these sectors manages the international radio frequency spectrum and satellite orbit resources?
explanation: 'ITU-R (Radiocommunication) … manages the international radio frequency spectrum and satellite orbit resources.'

question_text: ______ regulation gives regulation its power to react reasonably in unforeseen circumstances.
options: nemo judex in sua causa debet esse
explanation: Reacting reasonably to unforeseen circumstances is ex-post regulation — you respond after events occur, unlike fixed ex-ante rules.

question_text: In the mixed economy
options: economic problems are solved by the government and market
economic decisions are made by the private sector and free market
economic allocation is achieved by the 'invisible hand'
economic questions are solved by government departments
correct_answer: economic problems are solved by the government and market
explanation: A mixed economy blends command and market: 'Command measures, blended with market economies, create the mixed economies,' with governments intervening to correct market failure.

question_text: Which of these sectors helps spread equitable, sustainable and affordable access to information and communication technologies (ICT)?
explanation: 'ITU-D (Development) … helps spread equitable, sustainable and affordable access to information and communication technologies (ICT).'

question_text: The specialized agency of the United Nations (UN) responsible for issues that concern information and communication technologies is
options: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
Institute of Electrical and Electronic Engineers
explanation: The UN's ICT agency is the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) — note the official name uses the singular 'Telecommunication'.

question_text: Which of these types of economies is vulnerable to managerial corruption?
explanation: The deck: the command economy 'fails because of … vulnerability to managerial corruption' (and the intractable complexity of central control).

question_text: The principles of good regulatory decision-making include all of the following EXCEPT
explanation: Transparency, Objectivity and Professionalism are all listed principles, so none of the three is an exception.

question_text: A change in price can cause a shift of a demand curve.
explanation: FALSE. A change in the good's own price is a movement ALONG the demand curve. The curve only shifts when income, prices of related goods, taste, expectations or the number of buyers change.

question_text: A command economy decides resource allocation by government planning.
explanation: TRUE. 'In a command economy a powerful agent (usually the government) determines what people will produce, earn and consume.'

question_text: What type of rules are vulnerable to becoming dated or inappropriate in a fast-moving high technology industry?
options: nemo judex in sua causa debet esse
explanation: Ex-ante rules are fixed in advance, so in a fast-moving high-tech industry they quickly become dated or inappropriate.

question_text: If a price increase of good A increases the quantity demanded of good B, then good B is a
explanation: If A's price rises and B's quantity demanded rises, buyers are switching from A to B — they are substitutes (positive cross-price relationship).

question_text: What type of rule is being applied if a regulator states, 'You must not indulge in anti-competitive practice', but determines whether a breach has taken place after the event?
options: nemo judex in sua causa debet esse
explanation: Determining whether a breach occurred AFTER the event is ex-post regulation (ex post = 'after some issues have already occurred').

question_text: Opponents of ______ regulation believe that it gives regulators the combined functions of lawmaker, policeman, judge, jury and executioner.
options: nemo judex in sua causa debet esse
explanation: Inferred: this classic criticism — one body that writes the rules, enforces them and judges breaches — is levelled at ex-ante (prescriptive, sector-specific) regulation, as opposed to ex-post competition law adjudicated by the courts. NB: not stated verbatim in the decks and un-highlighted in the key, so confirm.

question_text: Price ceilings are imposed to increase price above the free market equilibrium price.
explanation: FALSE. A price ceiling holds the price BELOW equilibrium (a maximum price); it is a price FLOOR that keeps price above equilibrium.

question_text: The principle ______ ensures that no person can judge a case in which they have an interest.
options: nemo judex in sua causa debet esse
correct_answer: nemo judex in sua causa debet esse
explanation: 'No one should be a judge in their own cause' is the maxim nemo judex in sua causa debet esse — the rule against bias.

question_text: The role of regulators changes as markets become more competitive.
explanation: TRUE — as competition develops the regulator's role shifts (lighter-touch / more ex-post competition oversight).

question_text: Which of these sectors standardizes global telecommunications (except for radio)?
explanation: 'ITU-T (Standardization) … standardizes global telecommunications (except for radio)'; radio is ITU-R's job.

question_text: By concentrating action on proven grievances rather than on compliance with finely detailed rules, ______ regulation is potentially efficient regulation.
options: nemo judex in sua causa debet esse
explanation: Ex-post regulation acts on proven grievances after the fact instead of via finely detailed pre-set rules; the deck notes 'intrusion can be lessened by the use of ex-post rules.'
